chapter: Band building and learning from musicians
title: Pride and confidence of the New Orleans musicians
summary: DeVore describes the tremendous pride and love of music beneath Jim Robinson's clowning and the other New Orleans men.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

All right, let's see. We're talking about how these men have pride in what they've done. Well, they have a tremendous amount of pride. It's not exactly on the surface, you know, and they'll kid around and bark to music like Jim, you know, it seems like he's clowning around everything, but when you get right down to brass tacks, man, these men love music and they have a tremendous amount of pride in their, in the way that they do things. All the New Orleans men have. That's the thing that struck me after I got to know them for a while. It wouldn't, they'd be almost, it seems to me when I first met them.
